title: Localizing subcategories are independent of larger existing coproduct indices
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive pretriangulated category with a zero object, integer shifts and additive shift functors. Suppose every morphism set is equivalent to a type in universe $s$ [def-weil-preadditive-category, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P$ be a property of objects satisfying $\operatorname{IsLocalizingSubcategoryOfSize}_s(P)$ of [sk-def-localizing-closure]: it is replete, triangulated, and closed under all existing coproducts indexed by types in universe $s$. Then $P$ is closed under all existing coproducts indexed in the object universe, and hence satisfies $\operatorname{IsLocalizingSubcategory}(P)$. This does not assert existence of any coproduct.

proof.text: For a coproduct with inclusions i_k, construct p_k from the family with identity at k and zero elsewhere. On nonzero indices the endomorphisms p_k followed by i_k are distinct: test an equality for k≠l by precomposition with i_k and postcomposition with p_k to obtain id(K_k)=0, a contradiction. Thus the nonzero indices inject into the small endomorphism set of the vertex.

Restrict the cofan to nonzero summands. Extend any cocone by zero on the omitted summands to prove its colimit universal property at the same vertex. Reindex the support through Shrink and use P closure for s-indexed coproducts. The replete and triangulated clauses are exactly those assumed; this proves the large-index closure, including empty support.
